title: Subscription Total Kept Fee And Credit As Separate Signs
text: id: COMP-012 domain: math title: Subscription Total Kept Fee And Credit As Separate Signs tags: money, subscription, credit memory: A subscription total once drifted because I treated a credit like another fee. I wrote monthly cost times months, then setup fee as a plus, then the credit as a minus with the word credit still beside it. Seeing the signs separately kept the final price honest. The bill matched when the credit stayed negative.

title: Credit Stayed Visible As Minus Ten Credit
text: id: COMP-025 domain: math title: Credit Stayed Visible As Minus Ten Credit tags: subscription, credit, money, sign memory: I once subtracted a credit correctly but wrote the line so vaguely that another person could not tell where the discount went. The repaired version kept the words and sign together: minus 10 credit. In subscription totals, monthly charge times months came first, setup fee stayed positive, and the credit was subtracted exactly once. After the credit had been applied, I did not subtract it again.

title: Tiered Pricing Split Base Units Extra Units Fixed Fee
text: id: COMP-001 domain: math title: Tiered Pricing Split Base Units Extra Units Fixed Fee tags: tiered-pricing, units, addition memory: I once answered a tiered utility bill too quickly and charged every unit at the blended-looking rate. The correction was embarrassing because the structure was simple: first tier, extra units, fixed fee. I rewrote it as 100 base units, then units above 100, then the fixed charge. The revised bill matched the invoice exactly, and I remembered how a tier problem punishes shortcuts.
